findings.description: The new readBrief hint ("Remove it, then run `pup brief edit` to start a new one.") is wrong in two cases where brief.md is a regular file with one link: a file over 1 MiB, which readPlainFile refuses, and a file that raises EACCES. ensureBrief accepts both, so `pup brief edit` could fix them in place, but the hint tells the operator to delete the file and lose their text. Keep the link and non-regular-file refusal separate from size or permission failures, for example by lstat-ing in the catch the way ensureBrief does, and give the oversize case its existing 'shorten it with `pup brief edit`' wording.

The new catch-block comment in `brief edit` restates what the InvalidProfileError check and `refuse(error.message)` already show. Only the pointer to decisions 57 and 194 adds anything, so it could shrink to e.g. `// decisions 57, 194: refuse in one line, as show does`.

This is the fifth copy in src/cli/index.ts of 'catch, rethrow unless InvalidProfileError, refuse(error.message)'; the others are near lines 1189, 1455, 1494 and 1730. This copy also forces the split `let path; let created;` declaration. A small local helper such as `refuseInvalidProfile(() => ensureBrief(repoPath))` that returns undefined after refusing would remove both.

process_issues.description: review-security was not spawned: the change only adds a catch-and-refuse around an existing InvalidProfileError throw and rewords one message, so no trust boundary is touched.
review-guards could not run scripts/adr-index.sh under the CI Bash lock, so its ADR invariant check was a grep of docs/adr/ rather than a full index read.
